qt: to the Commission Sebastian Kruis (PfE) Subject:

In January 2023, a framework contract on tobacco control was awarded by the Commission, through the European Health and Digital Executive Agency, to a consortium led by Open Evidence, of which ENSP is a member. In February 2023, a post by Nofumadores representatives on the European Citizens’ Initiative Forum stated that Nofumadores and ENSP wanted to gradually end tobacco and nicotine product sales in the EU. Clearing the Air reported that minutes of an April 2023 meeting between ENSP and DG SANTE showed that they discussed changes to the Tobacco Products Directive1. Following a complaint in March 2024, the Ombudsman closed case 517/2024/FA on 4 February 2025, accepting the Commission’s assessment but criticising its failure to explain how it assessed ENSP’s interest in tobacco control. 1.
How did the Commission apply its conflict-of-interest rules to ENSP’s participation? What safeguards were adopted?
Were the April 2023 meeting minutes provided to the Ombudsman before the case was closed? If so, when? If not, for what reason?
What safeguards does the Commission apply across its policy areas to prevent EU funding from financing NGO lobbying that reinforces its own proposals?

Directive 2014/40/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 3 April 2014 on the approximation of the laws, regulations and administrative provisions of the Member States concerning the manufacture, presentation and sale of tobacco and related products and repealing Directive 2001/37/EC, OJ L 127, 29.4.2014, p. 1, ELI: http://data.europa.eu/eli/dir/2014/40/oj. 1
